title: EIA raises November natural gas storage forecast after warm start to month
summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) expects almost 70 billion cubic feet more natural gas to be in U.S. storage at the end of November than it forecast in October. A warm start to the month is easing pressure on natural gas prices.

title: EIA expects a mixed picture for winter fuel costs this year
summary: In the 2026-27 Winter Fuels Outlook, released alongside the October Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO), the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) expects U.S. households that primarily heat with natural gas or propane - about half of households - will spend less on energy expenses this winter than last winter. title: EIA expects record electricity generation in 2026 and 2027
summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) expects U.S. electricity generation will grow 2.2% to a record 4,368 billion kilowatthours (BkWh) this year. EIA expects an additional 1.7% growth in electricity generation next year.

title: EIA expects highest natural gas inventories in a decade heading into winter
summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration expects natural gas inventories will increase to 3,985 billion cubic feet (Bcf) in October, the most gas in inventories ahead of the winter heating season since 2016.

title: EIA increases global oil production forecast after the opening of the Strait of Hormuz
summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration published its July Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO), increasing its expectations for global oil production.

title: EIA expects a drop in global oil demand will limit price increases from Hormuz disruptions
summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration published its June Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO), reducing its expectation for global oil demand in 2026. title: EIA updates forecast amid continued Mideast disruption; will publish new energy security datasets
summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration published its May Short-Term Energy Outlook, reflecting a continued disruption to Middle Eastern oil flows.

title: EIA releases the Annual Energy Outlook 2026
summary: The Annual Energy Outlook 2026 (AEO2026) explores medium- and long-term alternative futures in the United States through 2050. title: Hormuz closure and related production outages are key drivers in EIA's latest forecast
summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration published its April Short Term Energy Outlook this week, examining the implications of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

title: EIA launches pilot survey on energy use at data centers
summary: EIA is launching three voluntary pilot field studies to evaluate energy consumption in data centers, with web-based pilot surveys in Texas and Washington state as well as in-person interviews in Northern Virginia and Washington, DC.
